title: Finite-field internal Hom has a bounded etale model with its Tor interval
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] which is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $A$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$ with its discrete condensed structure [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $A_X=p_X^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], identified with the constant ring sheaf. Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Work in ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves and with ambient relative derived internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $C_P,C_Q\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ be bounded étale complexes whose cohomology sheaves admit finite constructible locally closed stratifications with locally constant finite-dimensional $A$-values [def-pe-etale-constructible-module]. Set $P=\nu_X^*C_P$, $Q=\nu_X^*C_Q$ and $J=R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(P,Q)$.

The complexes $P,Q,J$ have bounded cohomology constructible in the finite constant local-model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. There exists a bounded cochain complex $D^\bullet$ of étale $A$-module sheaves, with constructible finite-dimensional cohomology, and an isomorphism in the derived category
$$\nu_X^*D^\bullet\simeq J.$$
Moreover, for every cohomological interval $[a,b]$, $a\le b$, containing the cohomology of $J$, this same $D^\bullet$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: for every degree-zero étale $A$-module sheaf $N$ one has
$$H^q(D^\bullet\otimes_A^L N)=0\qquad(q\notin[a,b]).$$
In particular $D^\bullet$ has finite Tor amplitude. The ground field $k$ need not be finite, perfect or separably closed, and neither input is assumed site-perfect.

proof.text: The field $A$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$. The assumed qcqs hypotheses therefore allow the constructible comparison theorem [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] with coefficients $A$. Its forward bounded-constructible equivalence sends $C_P,C_Q$ to $P,Q$. More explicitly, exactness of $\nu_X^*$ [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] give $H^q(P)\cong\nu_X^*H^q(C_P)$ and the analogous formula for $Q$, so their cohomological bounds are preserved. The sheaf part of the comparison theorem makes these cohomology sheaves constructible. That theorem's constructibility is local on $X$; to get the single finite stratification required for qcqs $X$, choose a finite affine open cover $U_1,\dots,U_n$ with stratifications $U_i=\coprod_aZ_{ia}$ and use the strata $Z_{ia}\cap(U_i\setminus\bigcup_{j<i}U_j)$. They are locally closed in $X$, hence constructible, because $X$ is of finite type over a field and so Noetherian, as remarked in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. A local model restricts to each smaller stratum, since pulling back $\Lambda_U\otimes P$ gives the same form. For $A_X$ the constant field sheaf, the local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] agree with locally constant finite-dimensional $A$-values: a finite-dimensional vector space is $A^r$, whose scalar extension is $A_X^r$, and every finitely presented $A$-module is finite-dimensional. Thus this is exactly the finite constant local-model constructibility required in the conclusion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-internal-hom-finiteness] to these $P,Q$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given prime $\ell$, arbitrary characteristic-$p$ base field $k$ with $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $X$, finite field $A$ of characteristic $\ell$, and the bounded finite constant local-model inputs established in step 1. It follows that the ambient relative internal Hom $J=R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(P,Q)$ is bounded and constructible in the same sense. This application requires neither site-perfect inputs nor a restriction on the ground field beyond the stated characteristic.

proof.text: Apply essential surjectivity of the bounded constructible derived equivalence in [sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison] to $J$. The hypotheses remain qcqs $X$ and discrete Noetherian $A$, and step 2 supplies the target object's bounded constructibility. We obtain $C\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ and an isomorphism $e:\nu_X^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}J$. Over the finite field $A$, finite type of each local module means finite-dimensionality. This uses only the comparison theorem's stated equivalence; it does not assert that inverse image commutes with internal Hom.

proof.text: Choose integers $u\le v$ containing the cohomology of $C$. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-representative] in the abelian category of étale $A$-module sheaves. It gives a cochain complex $D^\bullet$ zero outside $[u,v]$ and an isomorphism $d:Q(D^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ in the derived category. The isomorphism identifies $H^q(D^\bullet)$ with $H^q(C)$, so these sheaves are constructible with finite-dimensional local values. Composing $\nu_X^*d$ with $e$ gives $\nu_X^*D^\bullet\simeq J$. Fix this $D^\bullet$ and these isomorphisms before choosing an interval in the next step.

Let $a\le b$ be any integers with $H^q(J)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. The constant-field result [lem-sfb-constant-field-tor-bounds], applied to $J$ with $\kappa=A$, says that $J$ has Tor amplitude in this same interval against every degree-zero pro-étale $A_X$-module. Since $e$ is an isomorphism, tensoring it with any test module gives an isomorphism on tensor products and hence on cohomology; thus $\nu_X^*C$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Apply the reflection direction of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] to $C\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$: $X$ is qcqs and $A$ is discrete Noetherian, exactly its assumptions. It gives $H^q(C\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for every degree-zero étale module $N$ and $q\notin[a,b]$. Tensoring $d:Q(D^\bullet)\simeq C$ with $N$ identifies these groups with $H^q(D^\bullet\otimes_A^L N)$. This proves the required interval for the fixed $D^\bullet$. Since step 2 supplies at least one finite cohomological interval for $J$, it also proves finite Tor amplitude.
